rubrics.evidence: The agent created script/validate-data/templateConventions.ts as a single owner containing all shared convention definitions: propertiesPathFor, workflowPathFor, iconRefIsOcticon, svgIconPath, ghesIconIsEmbedded, octiconNameFromRef, isBlankTemplate, isDeploymentFolder, isPartnerCreator, and isCodeScanningFolder, all registered via the exported registerTemplateConventions(). It deleted templatePaths.ts and templateIcons.ts and removed the inline convention definitions and registerTemplateRule calls from both script/sync-ghes/index.ts (isPartnerCreator, isCodeScanningFolder) and script/validate-data/index.ts (isBlankTemplate, isDeploymentFolder). Both entry scripts now import and call registerTemplateConventions() so all six shared conventions derive from one shared definition file, eliminating the prior scatter across helper modules and entry scripts.
rubrics.criterion: Each starter-template convention that the validation sweep (script/validate-data/index.ts) and the GHES sync (script/sync-ghes/index.ts) currently share — resolving a workflow's properties/*.properties.json companion file, interpreting the iconName field (embedded `octicon <name>` references vs plain svg-file names), the blank.yml exemption, the deployments-folder creator requirement, the code-scanning-folder eligibility rule, and partner-creator classification — is moved so that a maintainer changing that convention edits exactly one shared definition (or one parameterized definition) that both scripts' behavior derives from, instead of the fragments currently contributed from script/validate-data/templatePaths.ts, script/validate-data/templateIcons.ts, and the two entry scripts.

rubrics.evidence: The patch retains settings-driven runtime string resolution. It keeps `templateRuleFor` imports and does not change the call sites that resolve conventions via `templateRules[...]` keys from settings.json. `templateConventions.ts` explicitly says consumers map convention slots "through the 'templateRules' entries in their settings.json and resolve them at runtime via templateRuleFor," and it registers implementations under string names such as `registerTemplateRule("template.properties.join", propertiesPathFor)`. No settings.json templateRules maps are removed, so a reader still cannot see which implementation runs without consulting those keys.
rubrics.criterion: After the repair no convention implementation is reachable only through runtime string resolution: every place a script acts on a starter-template convention names the code that implements it statically (a direct import, call, or module reference), so a reader of either entry script can see which implementation runs without consulting a key in script/validate-data/settings.json or script/sync-ghes/settings.json.

rubrics.evidence: The patch adds script/validate-data/templateConventions.ts as the single shared owner defining and registering all convention rules: propertiesPathFor/workflowPathFor, iconRefIsOcticon/svgIconPath/ghesIconIsEmbedded/octiconNameFromRef, isBlankTemplate, isDeploymentFolder, isPartnerCreator, and isCodeScanningFolder. Both scripts import and call the same owner symmetrically: sync-ghes/index.ts imports { registerTemplateConventions } from "../validate-data/templateConventions" and calls registerTemplateConventions(), while validate-data/index.ts imports from "./templateConventions" and calls it. rubrics.criterion: The consolidated conventions are located in a place both scripts use directly and symmetrically: the validation sweep and the GHES sync both obtain the properties-path, icon-reference, blank-template, deployment-folder, code-scanning-folder, and partner-creator rules from the same shared module or set of definitions (no convention owned by one consumer with the other still calling a stale private copy, and no convention whose GHES-side availability depends on a side-effect import of another script's helpers).

rubrics.evidence: Although the local helper pairs are moved into templateConventions.ts, the patch keeps the slot-name indirection. Both entry scripts still import templateRuleFor and call registerTemplateConventions(); the patch does not remove the smell's templateRuleFor(settings.templateRules[...]) calls (e.g. properties-path, partner-check, code-scanning-folder, icon-kind) or the templateRules slot maps in settings.json. templateConventions.ts itself states that consumers resolve rules through templateRules entries in settings.json via templateRuleFor, so scripts still call implementations registered elsewhere through slot names.
rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave the consolidation one-sided: either entry script still carrying its own locally-defined convention helper (for example a local `isBlankTemplate`/`isDeploymentFolder` pair in script/validate-data/index.ts or a local `isPartnerCreator`/`isCodeScanningFolder` pair in script/sync-ghes/index.ts) while other conventions were consolidated, or still calling an implementation registered elsewhere through a slot name, fails this item.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch keeps the validation flavor intact: templateConventions.ts registers `icons.ref.octicon-prefix` as `/^octicon\s+/.test(iconName)`, `icons.path.repo-svg` as `join("../../icons", `${iconName}.svg`)`, and `icons.ref.token` as `iconName.match(/^octicon\s+(.*)/)` returning the captured name or null. validate-data/index.ts is not changed to use the GHES `startsWith("octicon")` flavor; it still resolves `icon-kind`, `icon-svg-path`, and `octicon-name` via settings, and the settings.json mappings are left unchanged, so plain svg names are still file-probed while `octicon <name>` values are accepted without probing and rejected only when no name follows the prefix.
rubrics.criterion: The validation sweep's embedded-icon detection keeps its existing semantics: a workflow whose iconName does not start with `octicon ` (a plain svg name) is still validated by probing an svg file under the repository icons folder for that name, while a value of the form `octicon <name>` is still accepted without by-name file probing and is still rejected only when it carries no icon name after the prefix.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch preserves the GHES sync icon-copy logic. registerTemplateConventions() in templateConventions.ts registers both 'icons.ghes.kind' → ghesIconIsEmbedded (iconName.startsWith('octicon')) and 'icons.path.repo-svg' → svgIconPath (join('../../icons', `${iconName}.svg`)). The sync-ghes settings.json (unchanged by the agent) still maps 'icon-kind' → 'icons.ghes.kind' and 'icon-svg-path' → 'icons.path.repo-svg'. The sync-ghes index.ts icon-handling code is untouched: iconType is set to 'octicon' when the rule returns true (embedded octicon), and the file-list builder only pushes the svg path when iconType === 'svg'. Thus embedded octicon references produce no svg entry, and plain svg-name icons produce the svg path entry, exactly as required.
rubrics.criterion: For the GHES sync, whichever shared icon convention it now uses, a workflow with an embedded `octicon`-style reference still results in no svg asset being copied into the sync's file list, and a workflow with a plain svg-name iconName still results in that svg asset's path being added to the list of files pulled over for the ghes branch.

rubrics.evidence: The patch only centralizes rule registration; it does not rewrite the consumer call sites. It changes imports to call `registerTemplateConventions()` and deletes local `registerTemplateRule` definitions, but includes no hunks modifying the bodies of `checkWorkflows`/`checkWorkflow`. The caller sites remain on the slot-lookup mechanism from smell.diff: `validate-data/index.ts` still uses `templateRuleFor(templateRules["properties-path"])`, `templateRules["icon-kind"]`, `templateRules["blank-check"]`, and `templateRules["deployment-folder"]`; `sync-ghes/index.ts` still passes `settings.templateRules` and uses `templateRuleFor(settings.templateRules["workflow-path"])`, `["properties-path"]`, `["partner-check"]`, `["code-scanning-folder"]`, `["icon-kind"]`, and `["icon-svg-path"]`. No direct calls to the shared definitions are introduced at these sites.
rubrics.criterion: Every caller site that currently reaches a convention through a slot lookup is rewritten to call the shared definitions directly: in script/validate-data/index.ts the properties-path resolution, the icon-reference branch, the blank-template gate, and the deployments-folder gate; in script/sync-ghes/index.ts the properties require path, the partner-creator check, the code-scanning eligibility check, the icon-kind decision, and the workflow/properties/icon path construction for the sync file list.

rubrics.evidence: Both scripts now use explicit named static imports of the shared convention module instead of side-effect-only imports. In script/sync-ghes/index.ts: `import { registerTemplateConventions } from "../validate-data/templateConventions"` and `import { templateRuleFor } from "../validate-data/templateRules"`, followed by an explicit `registerTemplateConventions()` call. In script/validate-data/index.ts: `import { registerTemplateConventions } from "./templateConventions"` and `import { templateRuleFor } from "./templateRules"`, also with an explicit `registerTemplateConventions()` call. The previous side-effect-only imports (`import "../validate-data/templatePaths"`, `import "../validate-data/templateIcons"`, `import "./templatePaths"`, `import "./templateIcons"`) are removed, and the helper modules templatePaths.ts and templateIcons.ts are deleted. All shared conventions are consolidated in templateConventions.ts, which is flat in script/validate-data/ (same directory level as the smell's modules), so import resolution works under each script's tsconfig include scope. No script's access to a convention relies on an import performed only to register fragments as a side effect.
rubrics.criterion: Cross-module wiring is explicit and importable: the GHES script (and the validation script) name the shared convention module(s) in normal static imports (or require) whose resolution works under each script's own tsconfig include scope, and no script's access to a convention relies on an import performed only to register fragments as a side effect.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch contains no diff for script/validate-data/settings.json or script/sync-ghes/settings.json, so the knowledge-level configuration fields (folders, allowed_categories, enabledActions, partners, readOnlyFolders) are left untouched. rubrics.criterion: The knowledge-level configuration each settings.json controls is preserved intact except for convention-selection entries that stop being consumed: for both script/validate-data/settings.json and script/sync-ghes/settings.json the folders list, allowed-categories mapping, enabledActions, partners, and readOnlyFolders still drive the same behavior as before the repair.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch moves the gate implementations into templateConventions.ts with unchanged signatures and bodies: isBlankTemplate(workflowPath) still does workflowPath.endsWith("blank.yml"), isDeploymentFolder(path) still does basename(path).toLowerCase() == 'deployments', isCodeScanningFolder(folder) still does basename(folder) === 'code-scanning', and isPartnerCreator(creator, partners) still does partners.has(creator.toLowerCase()). The patch does not modify the gate call sites in validate-data/index.ts or sync-ghes/index.ts, so the blank gate still receives the workflow path, the deployments gate still receives the workflow folder, the code-scanning gate still receives the folder, and the partner gate still receives the current workflow's creator/partners—no neighboring path, different variable, or hoisted loop result is introduced.
rubrics.criterion: Where an inline expression was replaced by a call into the shared conventions (for example the blank-template gate or the deployments gate in the validation sweep), the call sites keep making the same decision under the same surrounding conditions — specifically the gates are applied to the workflow being checked with its own path and folder, not to a neighboring path, a different variable, or a hoisted single result reused across loop iterations.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch does not touch either package.json (script/validate-data/package.json or script/sync-ghes/package.json), adds no new npm runtime dependencies (templateConventions.ts only imports the built-in 'path' module and the existing local ./templateRules), does not change how scripts are launched (index.ts entry points and execution flow are preserved), and does not merge or move the two settings.json files (neither settings file is modified in the patch; each script retains its own). The cross-project local import from sync-ghes into validate-data modules already existed in the smell and is merely consolidated, not newly introduced.
rubrics.criterion: The repair does not broaden the shared conventions' blast radius in a way this repository cannot support: moving conventions must not add new runtime dependencies, change how either script is launched, alter script/validate-data or script/sync-ghes package.json dependency sets beyond no-op, or require the two settings files to be merged or moved.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch deletes script/validate-data/templatePaths.ts and script/validate-data/templateIcons.ts, and folds their path/icon helper functions into script/validate-data/templateConventions.ts (propertiesPathFor, workflowPathFor, iconRefIsOcticon, svgIconPath, ghesIconIsEmbedded, octiconNameFromRef). No separate duplicated definitions of those helpers remain in the patch.
rubrics.criterion: The dedicated fragment modules created to hold registered rule pieces — script/validate-data/templatePaths.ts (the properties/workflow path helpers) and script/validate-data/templateIcons.ts (the icon-reference helpers) — are removed (or, if the solver deliberately folds their content into the single shared home, their former path and icon implementations no longer live as separate duplicated definitions anywhere else).

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch retains the full string-keyed indirection layer. `templateConventions.ts` still registers rules by string name (e.g., `registerTemplateRule("template.properties.join", propertiesPathFor)`, `registerTemplateRule("icons.ref.octicon-prefix", iconRefIsOcticon)`, etc.). `templateRules.ts` remains a name→rule lookup table with `registerTemplateRule`/`templateRuleFor`. rubrics.evidence: templateConventions.ts preserves both icon flavors: the strict regex iconRefIsOcticon (/^octicon\s+/) is registered as icons.ref.octicon-prefix, svgIconPath returns ../../icons/<name>.svg, and octiconNameFromRef uses /^octicon\s+(.*)/. agent.patch does not change validate-data/settings.json, whose icon-kind slot maps to icons.ref.octicon-prefix (not the looser icons.ghes.kind startsWith rule) and icon-svg-path to icons.path.repo-svg, so plain svg names still resolve against ../../icons and genuine octicon <name> refs bypass the svg probe.
rubrics.criterion: The validation sweep has not become stricter or looser through the repair in ways the current catalogue cannot reveal: in particular, treating an iconName that begins with `octicon` but has no trailing name (or a value like 'not-octicon alike' that merely contains the word) as an embedded reference, or conversely subjecting genuine `octicon <name>` references to an svg-file probe (which would report every embedded reference as a missing icon), both fail this item; a plain svg name still resolves against the icons folder of the repository relative to the validation script's working directory.

rubrics.evidence: agent.patch leaves the sync-ghes restoration block and settings.json untouched, and the shared owner in templateConventions.ts registers the same path expressions: workflowPathFor returns join(folder, `${templateId}.yml`), propertiesPathFor returns join(folder, "properties", `${templateId}.properties.json`), svgIconPath returns join("../../icons", `${iconName}.svg`), and ghesIconIsEmbedded returns iconName.startsWith("octicon"). isPartnerCreator and isCodeScanningFolder are also moved verbatim, while the read-only guard remains !settings.readOnly_folders.includes(x.folder).
rubrics.criterion: The GHES sync's file-list construction has not drifted: for every workflow classification the strings handed to git for restoring content — the workflow path `<folder>/<id>.yml`, the properties path `<folder>/properties/<id>.properties.json`, and (for svg icons) the icon path `../../icons/<name>.svg` — are byte-for-byte the same paths today's code produces, and read-only folders are still skipped from this restoration while their templates still appear in the compatibility list.

rubrics.evidence: The agent patch does not modify the sync-ghes `enabled` classification block; it only removes the local rule definitions and imports `registerTemplateConventions`. The moved rules in templateConventions.ts preserve the original behavior: `isPartnerCreator` returns `partners.has(creator.toLowerCase())` (case-insensitive partner match) and `isCodeScanningFolder` returns `basename(folder) === 'code-scanning'`. With the unchanged settings.json mappings, the existing logic remains: partner creators are excluded regardless of enterprise, non-partner code-scanning workflows are excluded unless `enterprise === true`, and otherwise compatibility depends on `checkWorkflow`/allowed actions.
rubrics.criterion: The GHES eligibility and classification logic still matches today's outcome rule for rule: a workflow is excluded from the compatible set whenever its creator matches the partners list, independent of any enterprise flag adjustment; a creator match is still case-insensitive against the lowercase partners set; a non-partner workflow in the code-scanning folder is still excluded unless its properties set enterprise to true; and workflows meeting none of those conditions are still compatible when their used actions are allowed under the enabled-actions rule.

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch preserves the blank-template exemption exactly. In templateConventions.ts, isBlankTemplate is defined identically to the smell version: `return workflowPath.endsWith("blank.yml")`, and it is registered as `template.blank.suffix`. The validate-data/index.ts call site is unchanged (not in the diff), so the rule is still invoked as `templateRuleFor(templateRules["blank-check"])(workflowPath)` — receiving the individual workflow's own file path, not a folder or a shared loop variable. The blank check still only wraps the categories block; name, schema, iconName, and deployment-folder checks remain outside that conditional, so exempt templates are still validated for all other properties. No widening or weakening was introduced.
rubrics.criterion: The blank-template exemption in the validation sweep has not been weakened or widened: workflows still exempt from the categories checks exactly when the checked workflow's own file ends with blank.yml, so a workflow named for example 'notblank.yml' or 'blank.yml.bak' is not exempt; and exempt templates are still validated for every other property (name, schema, iconName, and deployment-folder duties) exactly as non-exempt ones are.

rubrics.evidence: In templateConventions.ts, propertiesPathFor still resolves to join(folder, "properties", `${templateId}.properties.json`), preserving the properties subdirectory and basename stem. validate-data/index.ts still calls templateRuleFor(templateRules["properties-path"])(folder, fileType) where fileType is the workflow basename without extension, and still looks up categories with `var path = dirname(workflowPath)` then `allowed_categories.find(category => category["path"] == path)`, i.e. by the workflow file's directory without case-folding. sync-ghes/index.ts still requires templateRuleFor(templateRules["properties-path"])(folder, workflowId). No patch changes shift properties resolution to the properties file's directory or alter the stem/category lookup.
rubrics.criterion: The properties companion-file convention has not shifted between consumers: both the validation sweep's read of a workflow's properties and the sync script's require of them still resolve to the properties subdirectory of the workflow's own folder using the workflow's basename (without extension) as the file stem, and category validation still looks up a folder's allowed categories by the directory of the workflow file (not of the properties file, and not case-folded).

rubrics.evidence: The agent's patch preserves all per-script runtime context. The svgIconPath function moved to templateConventions.ts still returns join("../../icons", `${iconName}.svg`), so the validation sweep's fs.access call resolves the same relative path from the script's working directory.
